reference.source: Dhingra Diseases of ENT 8th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Progressive solids dysphagia plus weight loss scopes urgently
Zenker pouch: elderly, undigested regurgitation, barium diagnosis
Globus has no true dysphagia or alarm features
Plummer Vinson: iron deficiency plus postcricoid web
reference.pathophysiology: Failed upper sphincter relaxation or pharyngeal weakness leaves residue aspirating after swallow, while distal obstruction or absent peristalsis with non relaxing lower sphincter (achalasia myenteric loss) stagnates food above stomach.
additionalDifferentials: Transfer versus transit dysphagia by immediate symptoms
Achalasia bird beak versus cancer pseudoachalasia (age, short history)
Globus versus dysphagia by meal relation
additionalInvestigations: Urgent gastroscopy with biopsies for alarm dysphagia
Barium swallow for pouch and motility outline, manometry for achalasia
Videofluoroscopy or FEES for oropharyngeal swallow
